expected_output.reasoning: The agent's response explains that tool definitions in a target are validated/loaded as a single unit (one array, validated as a whole), so an invalid tool fails the entire target, causing the whole tool list for that target to disappear. It identifies specific kinds of schema defects responsible: missing 'type: object' in inputSchema/outputSchema, missing required fields (name, description, inputSchema), unsupported property types, 'required' referencing undefined properties, malformed JSON, and name collisions/invalid tool names. It also tells the user how to find the offending definition: run get-gateway-target and inspect 'status' and 'statusReasons', which typically names the offending tool or field, and recommends validating JSON structure or isolating tools into separate targets. This covers all the key elements of the expected output: validation as a set causing whole-target failure, identification of defect types (unsupported types, missing required fields, name collisions), and guidance on finding the offending definition.

assertion_results.text: The response explains why one bad tool definition can fail the entire target rather than being skipped
assertion_results.evidence: "a target is a single unit, not a set of independent tools... all tool definitions go in one array... The gateway validates and loads it as a whole when you create or update the target... If the target isn't READY, the gateway has nothing to list for it, so your existing tools go missing along with the new one."
assertion_results.reasoning: The response clearly explains the architectural reason (single array, per-target validation and status) for why one bad tool fails the whole target instead of being skipped individually.

assertion_results.text: The response names a specific class of schema defect to look for

assertion_results.reasoning: The response lists multiple specific classes of schema defects (missing type:object, unsupported field types, mismatched required entries, missing required fields like name/description/inputSchema), satisfying the assertion of naming specific schema defect classes.

assertion_results.text: The response gives a concrete way to isolate the offending tool
assertion_results.evidence: "Run get-gateway-target on the failing target and read status and statusReasons. That text usually names the offending tool or field."
assertion_results.reasoning: The response provides a concrete, actionable method (running get-gateway-target and inspecting status/statusReasons) to isolate the offending tool, which directly satisfies the assertion.
